title: Guidelines for representing your business on Google

facts.fact: A business may create a Google Business Profile if it has a physical location customers can visit or travels to customers where they are.
facts.quote: If your business either has a physical location that customers can visit, or travels to customers where they are, you can create a Business Profile on Google.

facts.fact: Google's guidelines state there should be only one Business Profile per business.
facts.quote: There should only be one profile per business, as this can cause problems with how your information displays on Google Maps and Search.

facts.fact: Google's guidelines advise choosing the fewest number of categories needed to describe the business's overall core business.
facts.quote: Choose the fewest number of categories it takes to describe your overall core business.

facts.fact: Google's guidelines state that no links of any type are allowed in a business description.
facts.quote: No links of any type are allowed.

facts.fact: Google's guidelines state that business descriptions must not focus on special promotions, prices, or offer sales.
facts.quote: Focus on special promotions, prices, and offer sales

facts.fact: Google's guidelines state that including special characters or irrelevant legal terms in a business name requires real-world proof, such as signage, business cards, or invoices.
facts.quote: you must provide real-world proof (e.g.signage, business cards, invoices)

facts.fact: Google's business name rules state that the name must not include marketing taglines, store codes, trademark signs, fully capitalized words, business hours, phone numbers or URLs, service information, or location information.
facts.quote: Your name must not include:

facts.fact: Google's guidelines state that including unnecessary information in a business name is not permitted and could result in suspension of the Business Profile.
facts.quote: Including unnecessary information in your business name isn't permitted, and could result in the suspension of your Business Profile.

facts.fact: Google's guidelines state that P.O. boxes or mailboxes located at remote locations are not acceptable as a business address.
facts.quote: P.O. boxes or mailboxes located at remote locations aren't acceptable.

facts.fact: Google's guidelines state that a virtual office, where a business rents a mailing address but does not operate from that location, is not eligible for a Business Profile.
facts.quote: If your business rents a physical mailing address but doesn't operate out of that location, also known as a virtual office, that location isn't eligible for a Business Profile.

facts.fact: Google's guidelines state a co-working space office can be listed only if it maintains clear signage, receives customers during business hours, and is staffed by business staff during business hours.
facts.quote: Businesses can't list an office at a co-working space unless that office maintains clear signage

facts.fact: Google's guidelines state that businesses may post their own contact information (social media handles, email, phone number) on their own profile or in responses, but soliciting personal or confidential information is not allowed.
facts.quote: Merchants are permitted to post contact information (social media handles, email, phone number) for their own business

facts.fact: Google's guidelines state that if a mailbox or suite number must be specified, the physical address goes in Address Line 1 and the mailbox or suite number goes in Address Line 2.
facts.quote: Enter your physical address as "Address Line 1."

facts.fact: A service business with separate locations, each with its own service area and separate staff, is allowed one profile for each location.
facts.quote: If you have different locations for your service business, with separate service areas and separate staff at each location, you're allowed one profile for each location.

facts.fact: Google does not permit premium phone numbers on Business Profiles, regardless of the rate charged to the caller.
facts.quote: Premium phone numbers are not acceptable regardless of the rate charged to the caller.

facts.fact: Businesses associated with products or services that require customers to meet a minimum age, such as alcohol, cannabis, or weapons, aren't permitted as service-area businesses without a storefront.
facts.quote: Businesses associated with products or services that require the customer to be a certain minimum age, like alcohol, cannabis, or weapons, aren't permitted as service-area businesses without a storefront.

facts.fact: Google advises businesses not to create more than one page for each location of the business, whether in a single account or multiple accounts.
facts.quote: Do not create more than one page for each location of your business, either in a single account or multiple accounts.

facts.fact: For restaurants with multiple sets of hours, the guidelines say to use dine-in hours first, then takeout hours, then drive-through hours, and delivery hours as a last resort.
facts.quote: Use the hours when diners can sit down and dine in your restaurant. Otherwise, use takeout hours. If neither of those is possible, use drive-through hours, or, as a last resort, delivery hours.

facts.fact: Google advises businesses to use as few categories as possible to describe their core business and to make categories as specific as possible.
facts.quote: Use as few categories as possible to describe your overall core business from the provided list.

facts.fact: Businesses in an eligible country (US, CA, UK, and IE) can showcase in-store products on their Business Profile to turn online searchers into in-store shoppers.
facts.quote: If you run a retail business in an eligible country (US, CA, UK, and IE), you can turn online searchers into in-store shoppers by automatically showcasing your in-store products on your Business Profile.

facts.fact: Google's guidelines describe 2 kinds of menus: one for eating and drinking establishments and one for service businesses.
facts.quote: There are 2 kinds of menus:

facts.fact: Menus submitted for a business must list the complete set of items or services available, and sample menus that only list 'popular items' should not be submitted.
facts.quote: Sample menus that only list “popular items” (or similar excerpts) should not be submitted.

facts.fact: Menu URLs cannot be direct links to third-party ordering or delivery services.
facts.quote: Menu URLs can’t be direct links to third-party ordering or delivery services.

facts.fact: Google does not allow in-store product content related to alcohol, tobacco products, gambling, financial services, pharmaceuticals and unapproved supplements, or health or medical devices.
facts.quote: We do not allow content related to regulated products and services, including alcohol, tobacco products, gambling, financial services, pharmaceuticals and unapproved supplements, or health or medical devices.

facts.fact: Submitting products that violate Google's policy may result in removal of the entire product catalog, including products that aren't in violation.
facts.quote: Submitting products that violate Google's policy may result in removal of the entire product catalog, including products that aren't in violation.

facts.fact: Co-located businesses such as a restaurant inside a hotel, a pharmacy inside a supermarket, a gas station next to a supermarket, and a car rental at an airport with separate pick-up and drop-off should each have their own profile.
facts.quote: The following types of co-located businesses should each have their own profile.

facts.fact: All locations within the same country must have the same business name, with two listed exceptions.
facts.quote: There are 2 exceptions to this policy:

facts.fact: Locations of a single business must share the one category that best represents the business if they provide the same service.
facts.quote: All locations of a business must share the one category that best represents the business.

facts.fact: Delivery-only food brands are permitted if they have distinct branded packaging and a distinct website.
facts.quote: Delivery-only brands (i.e. those operating out of virtual kitchens) are permitted if they have distinct branded packaging and a distinct website.

facts.fact: Multiple virtual food brands operating out of one location are permitted but are subject to additional verification steps.
facts.quote: Multiple virtual brands operating out of one location are permitted, but are subject to additional verification steps.

facts.fact: Delivery-only food brands must add their service areas and hide their address on their Business Profile.
facts.quote: Delivery-only brands must add their service areas and [hide the address](https://support.google.com/business/answer/9157481?hl=en) on their business profile to avoid confusing their customers.

facts.fact: Third parties managing Business Profiles must notify the business owner and have their consent before submitting a menu URL for a business.
facts.quote: Third parties that manage Business Profiles on behalf of clients must notify and have the consent of the business owner to submit a menu URL for a business.

facts.fact: If a business changes its name but does not meet the page's criteria, Google considers it a new business, and the existing Business Profile must be marked as closed before a new profile is created under the new name.
facts.quote: If your business changes its name but doesn't meet the criteria above, then it's considered a new business. You must mark the existing Business Profile as closed

facts.fact: Google lists doctors, dentists, lawyers, financial planners, and insurance or real estate agents as examples of individual practitioners.
facts.quote: Doctors, dentists, lawyers, financial planners, and insurance or real estate agents are all individual practitioners.

facts.fact: A practitioner should not create multiple Business Profiles to cover all of their specializations.
facts.quote: A practitioner shouldn't have multiple Business Profiles to cover all of their specializations.

facts.fact: Sales associates or lead generation agents for corporations are not individual practitioners and are not eligible for a Business Profile.
facts.quote: Sales associates or lead generation agents for corporations aren't individual practitioners and aren't eligible for a Business Profile.

facts.fact: When a solo practitioner is the only public-facing practitioner at a location and represents a branded organization, the shared Business Profile should be named in the format '[brand/company]: [practitioner name]'.
facts.quote: Create a single Business Profile, named using the following format: [brand/company]: [practitioner name].

facts.fact: Publicly-facing departments that operate as distinct entities should have their own page, and each department's exact name must differ from the main business and other departments; such departments typically have a separate customer entrance and distinct categories.
facts.quote: Publicly-facing departments that operate as distinct entities should have their own page. The exact name of each department must be different from that of the main business

facts.fact: Auto dealers have specific and separate guidelines from the general Business Profile guidelines.
facts.quote: Auto dealers have specific and separate guidelines.

facts.fact: To take ownership of a Business Profile, a person first needs the previous owner to add them as an owner and then transfer ownership to them.
facts.quote: If you assume ownership of a Business Profile, you first need to have the previous owner add you as an owner and transfer ownership to you.

facts.fact: Google reserves the right to suspend access to Business Profiles on Google or other Google Services for individuals or businesses that violate its guidelines.
facts.quote: Google reserves the right to suspend access to Business Profiles on Google or other Google Services to individuals or businesses that violate these guidelines

facts.fact: Google's guidance says a business should not submit more than one reinstatement request for a suspended Google Business Profile listing.
facts.quote: (Note: Do not fill out more than one reinstatement request.)

facts.fact: When submitting a reinstatement request, Google's guidance says to upload photos of permanent business signage both outside and inside the building as proof of legitimacy.
facts.quote: uploading photos of your permanent business signage -- both outside and inside your building

facts.fact: Google's guidance lists a photo of a company vehicle with signage on it as proof for a Service Area Business seeking reinstatement.
facts.quote: a photo of a company vehicle with signage on it (if you’re a Service Area Business)

facts.fact: The page states that the support forum where this advice appears is run by volunteers, and that some are Google Business Profile Experts but are not Google employees.
facts.quote: This forum is run by volunteers. Some of us are Google Business Profile Experts. However, we are not Google employees.
